body:
Part of the `extract` feature. Plan source: task:a9d18cc6be1c2a2a note 17 (Task 1). Code locations are given by name, because line numbers have moved since the plan was written; check each one before using it.

Add `extract <symbols…> --to <module>`. It moves symbols to another module of the same project and keeps their identity and revision (Spec 1 §3 R1, R2). It runs in one transaction and is gated on `check_all`, like `submit`: if the result doesn't type-check, nothing changes.

**1. Decision first.** Add this at the end of `DECISIONS.md` with the next free number (D-102 is the last as of 2026-10-11, so likely **D-103**; check again). Then update Spec 1 §5's table (replace the Extract row, add E5002) and Spec 3 §2's command row that already lists `extract`.

> **D-103 `extract` moves symbols to another module or project.** Amends Spec 1 §5 (Aaron, 2026-10-10). `extract <symbols…> --to <module> [--to-project <folder>]` moves symbols with their identity and revision. It brings along private helpers that only they use, rewrites every remaining reference and import, moves tests that reach only moved code, and refuses a module or package dependency cycle with E5002, naming the boundary uses. `rename` changes only a symbol's name; `extract` changes its module or project. This replaces Spec 1 §5's Phase 1b Extract row. An operation that creates `derived-from` identities has no verb until one is needed. Why: an agent extracting components rewrote references by hand and a submit failed. The human chose `extract` over `move` and `rename`, accepting the change to Spec 1.

**2. Dispatch and docs.**
- Add an `extract` arm in `run_inner` (main.rs). The file `move` is handled earlier, in `lockdown::dispatch`, and is not touched.
- Add `extract` to the usage line, to `help`, and to the commands refused in investigations, reviews and strategy runs (`reference.txt` and the lockdown refusal list).
- The session-start reference must stay under 3,600 bytes (D-102 point 5): give `extract` one line there and put the worked example (point 13) in `help`.

**3. Operands.** Accept the forgiving forms; refuse the rest with a one-line message showing the right form.
- `--to src/solace_task.gleam` and `--to solace_task.gleam` are read as `solace_task`.
- `--to components/solace_task` is refused: `use --to solace_task --to-project ../components`.
- A module name in the symbol list is refused: `to move a whole module, use move src/x.gleam src/y.gleam`.
- Test symbols may go only to a test module (`*_test`); src→test and test→src are refused.
- The reply's first line echoes fully qualified names, so a surprising suffix match is visible.

**4. Resolution and idempotence.**
- A name that no longer resolves in the source but exists in the target gets `already in <target>`, and nothing changes.
- A name that resolves in both source and target is a collision: refuse and name it.
- Any other unresolved name gets E1001.
- Forgotten `--to-project`: when the target module doesn't exist here but exists in a project connected through gleam.toml path dependencies, refuse: `solace_task is in ../components; add --to-project ../components`. When a same-named module exists only in an unrelated project, create the module and add one reply line saying so.

**5. Helpers, constructors and visibility.**
- Helpers: fixpoint over `Index::used_by`. A private symbol whose users are all moving comes along.
- Constructors move with their type (`Index::build` indexes each constructor under its type).
- A moved symbol that staying code uses, or a staying symbol that moved code uses, becomes `pub` (new revision).
- Opaque types: refuse up front when a `pub opaque type` would be separated from code that constructs it or matches its constructors, e.g. `Task is opaque; its constructors are used by board.new_task, board.decode; extract them too`.

**6. Cycle refusal, E5002, at module level.** After the move the source imports the target when staying code uses moved code; the target imports the source when moved code uses staying code. If both, or if either new import closes a loop with existing imports, refuse. List every **direct boundary use** in one go (each staying symbol with the moved symbol that uses it) plus the closure size: `E5002 moved code uses 3 symbols that stay: lane_order (by Task.sort), … (moving them would bring 12 in total)`.

**7. Rewriting references, both directions.** One function computes "how module M refers to symbol X" and runs for every reference in staying code, moved code and tests.
- Staying code: bare `x` becomes `<target>.x`.
- Moved code: bare references to staying code become `<source>.x`; `<target>.x` becomes bare `x`.
- Unqualified imports stay unqualified: every item naming a moved symbol, type or constructor (including constructor-only `{Task}`), moves to an import of the target.
- Unused imports are removed afterwards; headers via `add_import` / `merge_import`.
- Columns: extend `gleam::scan` to return a column. First blank out string contents and comments with spaces, keeping newlines, so offsets match the original (`strip_comments` drops string contents today, which would shift columns).
- Collisions: never invent an alias. If the qualifier clashes with an existing import/alias, or is a local binding anywhere in the function, use the unqualified-import form there. If that name is also taken, refuse naming the module and clash. A name already defined in the target is refused.

**8. Dependent projects.** Projects whose gleam.toml depends on the source (e.g. `frontend` → `solace_board`) may use a moved `pub` symbol. Here, refuse and name those uses: `frontend.view uses solace_board.Task; extracting across projects comes with --to-project support`. The --to-project task adds rewriting them.

**9. Tests.** Use `reach::covered`. A test reaching only moved symbols moves to `test/<target>_test`; one also reaching staying code is rewritten in place. Test helpers follow the same fixpoint.

**10. Modules.** Create the target like `submit --new`. Retire an emptied source like `delete` does.

**11. History and undo.** Each moved symbol gets a `move` history entry with its old module. `board::record` keys rows by symbol id, so revert and cancel work unchanged.

**12. Lean reply.** Names and counts only, never bodies, in this order:
```
Moved solace_board.Task, solace_board.Notice (+3 helpers: lane_of, notice_text, column_name)
Now pub: column_name (new revision)
Rewrote 14 references in 3 modules
Tests moved: solace_board_test.task_round_trip -> solace_task_test
Not rewritten: suite solace_board.main no longer resolves; 12 places in 3 files (tests/board_acceptance.py:212, …)
```
- Suite entries in `checks` that stop resolving are always listed in full (today they're skipped silently in `reach::suites`).
- Watched-file hits match only qualified forms (`solace_board.Task`, `-m solace_board`); at most 5, then a count.

**13. Worked example** (in `help`): a refusal then the retry, with "extract a cohesive set in one call; the refusal lists everything to add."
```
extract board.Task --to solace_task
E5002 moved code uses 1 symbol that stays: lane_order (by Task.sort)
extract board.Task board.lane_order --to solace_task
```

**Tests (unit, main.rs):**
- Rewrites in each position: annotation, pattern, record update, constructor call, unqualified import (incl. `{Task}`), a reference after a string literal or trailing comment.
- Moved code: staying references become qualified; `target.x` becomes bare.
- Private helpers come along; a helper used from both sides becomes `pub`.
- Qualifier clashes with a local binding → unqualified form; a name taken in the target is refused.
- Module cycle refused with E5002 listing all boundary uses.
- Opaque type refused, naming constructor users.
- Test split: one moves, one rewritten in place.
- New target module created; emptied source retired.
- Repeat replies `already in`; failed type-check leaves the store unchanged.
- Operand refusals; forgotten `--to-project` refusal for a connected project.
- Dependent project's use refused, naming it; a suite that stops resolving is named.

**Checks:** `rust-unit`, `rust-acceptance`.
title: `extract`: move symbols to another module within one project
